entries.title: Learn poker with a small, free study path.
entries.description: Five self-paced sessions that turn free explanations into a hand record, a pot calculation and a decision you can explain.

entries.title: Study cash games without importing tournament assumptions.
entries.description: Separate cash-game costs, effective stacks and multiway decisions from tournament models, with a worked rake example.

entries.title: Omaha, lowball and mixed games: know which rules changed.
entries.description: Compare hand construction, low qualifiers and game rotations, then work through an Omaha hi-lo split-pot example.

entries.title: Choose a poker book or course you will actually use.
entries.description: Match prerequisites, format and one study goal before buying; distinguish author descriptions, independent reviews and free course material.

entries.title: A map of poker research, without the inflated claims.
entries.description: Find original research on regret, sampling, poker AI and evaluation, with explicit boundaries between game-solving results and playing strength.

entries.title: Poker math: the right number for the right question.
entries.description: Compare call prices, pure-bluff thresholds, minimum defense frequency and pot-limit raises with exact worked examples and a portable reference.

entries.title: Read the preflop chart before trusting the colors.
entries.description: Check game, position, stack convention, action history and combo weights before using a preflop chart as a study reference.

entries.title: Poker rules and fair play: find the right authority.
entries.description: Find live and online rule sources, understand minimum raises and software restrictions, and report concerns without unsupported accusations.

entries.title: Omaha hi-lo: play for a share, not just a low.
entries.description: Work through legal hand selection, quartering, counterfeiting and pot-share equity with complete fictional examples.

entries.title: Stud and lowball: change the rules before the strategy.
entries.description: Compare Stud8, razz, deuce-to-seven and Badugi, with worked hand comparisons and a rotation checklist.

entries.title: Multiway pots: count the opponents and the pots.
entries.description: Distinguish a better call price from a better hand, separate pot eligibility and avoid importing heads-up defense quotas.

entries.title: Turn a poker video or podcast into one useful lesson.
entries.description: Use annotated media starting points, distinguish transcripts from show notes and build a short study record without copying copyrighted material.

entries.title: Check the room, the rules and your protections.
entries.description: Find regulator and operator information, protect account access, preserve complaint records and reach support without gambling-site rankings.
